terms.name: Exoplanet (Extrasolar Planet)
terms.desc: A planet located outside our solar system that orbits a star other than the Sun.

terms.name: Habitable Zone (Goldilocks Zone)
terms.desc: The orbital region around a host star where planetary surface temperatures allow liquid water to exist.

terms.name: Transit Method
terms.desc: A detection technique that measures the periodic dip in a star's brightness when an orbiting exoplanet crosses in front of its stellar disk.

terms.name: Radial Velocity (Doppler Method)
terms.desc: A detection method measuring periodic Doppler shifts in a host star's spectrum caused by the gravitational tug of an orbiting exoplanet.

terms.name: Earth Similarity Index (ESI)
terms.desc: A scalar value ranging from 0 to 1 measuring how physically similar an exoplanet is to Earth in terms of radius, density, escape velocity, and surface temperature.

terms.name: Super-Earth
terms.desc: An extrasolar planet with a mass higher than Earth's but substantially below that of Uranus and Neptune (approx. 1.5 to 10 Earth masses).

terms.name: Mini-Neptune
terms.desc: A gas-rich planet with a thick hydrogen-helium atmosphere, smaller than Neptune but larger than Earth (approx. 2 to 4 Earth radii).

terms.name: Hot Jupiter
terms.desc: A class of giant gas exoplanets with physical characteristics similar to Jupiter, but orbiting very close to their parent stars (under 0.05 AU) with extreme surface temperatures.

terms.name: Tidal Locking
terms.desc: A state where an exoplanet's rotational period matches its orbital period, causing one side to perpetually face its star (eternal day) and the other to face away (eternal night).

terms.name: Stellar Host Spectral Class (O, B, A, F, G, K, M)
terms.desc: Classification of host stars by surface temperature and luminosity, from hot blue O-stars to cool red M-dwarfs.

terms.name: Transmission Spectroscopy
terms.desc: Analyzing starlight filtered through an exoplanet's atmosphere during a transit to identify atmospheric chemical biosignatures (water vapor, methane, ozone).

terms.name: HiPS (Hierarchical Progressive Surveys)
terms.desc: A standardized hierarchical tiling scheme based on HEALPix that allows smooth multi-resolution panning and zooming across petabyte-scale astronomical all-sky surveys.

terms.name: FITS (Flexible Image Transport System)
terms.desc: The standard open scientific file format used by astronomers to store, transmit, and process multi-dimensional data, spectra, and calibrated imagery.

terms.name: Aladin Lite
terms.desc: An interactive HTML5/WebGL celestial sky viewer developed by CDS (Strasbourg Astronomical Data Center) for exploring deep-sky images and catalogs.

terms.name: Emission Nebula
terms.desc: A cloud of high-temperature ionized gas that emits light of various optical wavelengths (such as the H-alpha red glow from hydrogen atoms energized by nearby hot stars).

terms.name: Reflection Nebula
terms.desc: A cloud of interstellar dust that reflects and scatters the light of nearby stars, typically appearing blue because shorter wavelengths scatter more efficiently.

terms.name: Planetary Nebula
terms.desc: An expanding glowing shell of ionized gas expelled by intermediate-mass stars during the late asymptotic giant branch phase of their evolution.

terms.name: Supernova Remnant (SNR)
terms.desc: The expanding diffuse, high-energy structural remnant resulting from the explosive destruction of a massive star.

terms.name: Open Cluster
terms.desc: A loosely bound group of up to a few thousand young stars formed from the same giant molecular cloud, usually found in galactic spiral arms.

terms.name: Globular Cluster
terms.desc: A tightly bound, spherical collection of hundreds of thousands to millions of ancient stars orbiting a galactic core.

terms.name: Redshift (z)
terms.desc: The displacement of spectral lines towards longer (redder) wavelengths in radiation from distant celestial bodies, proportional to recessional velocity caused by cosmic expansion.

terms.name: RA (Right Ascension) & Dec (Declination)
terms.desc: The standard equatorial celestial coordinate system: Right Ascension measures angular distance eastward along the celestial equator (in hours/minutes/seconds), and Declination measures angular distance north (+) or south (-) of the celestial equator (in degrees).

terms.name: SIMBAD & MAST Catalogs
terms.desc: Major astronomical databases: SIMBAD (CDS) provides cross-identifications and bibliography for celestial objects outside the solar system; MAST is the primary NASA data archive for JWST, Hubble, and Kepler missions.

terms.name: N-Body Gravitational Simulation
terms.desc: Numerical integration technique solving the classical equations of motion for N celestial bodies interacting with each other through mutual gravitational attraction.

terms.name: Keplerian Orbital Elements
terms.desc: Six fundamental mathematical parameters that uniquely describe the size, shape, and orientation of a celestial orbit (Semi-major axis, Eccentricity, Inclination, Longitude of ascending node, Argument of periapsis, True anomaly).

terms.name: Semi-Major Axis (a)
terms.desc: Half of the longest diameter of an elliptical orbit, defining the mean orbital distance of a body from its gravitational center (often measured in Astronomical Units, AU).

terms.name: Orbital Eccentricity (e)
terms.desc: A dimensionless parameter that determines the elongation of an orbit (0 = circular orbit, 0 < e < 1 = elliptical, e = 1 = parabolic, e > 1 = hyperbolic).

terms.name: Perihelion & Aphelion
terms.desc: The points in the orbit of a solar system body where it is closest to (perihelion) and farthest from (aphelion) the Sun.

terms.name: Lagrange Points (L1 – L5)
terms.desc: Five positions in an orbital configuration of two large bodies where the gravitational forces and centrifugal force produce a stable or quasi-stable point of equilibrium for a small third object (e.g. SOHO at Sun-Earth L1, JWST at Sun-Earth L2).

terms.name: Orbital Resonance
terms.desc: A dynamical condition where two orbiting bodies exert regular, periodic gravitational influence on each other because their orbital periods are related by a ratio of small integers.

terms.name: Mare (Maria)
terms.desc: A large, dark, basaltic plain on the Moon formed by ancient volcanic floods following asteroid impacts; Latin for "sea."

terms.name: Rima (Rille)
terms.desc: A long, narrow depression or trench in the lunar surface resembling a river canyon, formed by collapsed ancient subsurface lava tubes or graben faults.

terms.name: Statio
terms.desc: An official IAU landing site designation, used for historically significant locations such as Apollo crewed landing points and robotic landers.

terms.name: Oceanus
terms.desc: The Latin designation for "ocean"; uniquely assigned to Oceanus Procellarum, the largest mare plain on the Moon.

terms.name: Mons (Montes)
terms.desc: A lunar mountain or mountain range, frequently forming the elevated rims of ancient impact basins.

terms.name: Vallis
terms.desc: A lunar valley, carved by massive tectonic faulting or thermal lava channel carving.

terms.name: Rupes
terms.desc: A linear scarp or steep cliff formed by thrust faulting as the Moon cooled and contracted.

terms.name: Lunar Libration
terms.desc: The apparent slow rocking or oscillating motion of the Moon as viewed from Earth, allowing observers to see roughly 59% of the total lunar surface over time.

terms.name: Terminator
terms.desc: The moving dividing line between the sunlit day side and the dark night side of the Moon where surface topography casts the longest, most distinct shadows.

terms.name: Lunar Regolith
terms.desc: A fine, powdery layer of unconsolidated dust, broken rock fragments, and impact glass covering the solid bedrock of the lunar crust.

terms.name: Geologic Periods (Pre-Nectarian to Copernican)
terms.desc: The chronostratigraphic timeline of lunar evolution: Pre-Nectarian (>3.92 Ga), Nectarian (basin forming), Imbrian (mare basalt filling), Eratosthenian (crater degradation), and Copernican (bright ray crater systems).

terms.name: SDO AIA 171 Å
terms.desc: Extreme ultraviolet imaging channel (Fe IX, ~0.6–1.0 MK) revealing the quiet solar corona and intricate coronal magnetic loops.

terms.name: SDO AIA 304 Å
terms.desc: EUV filter (He II, ~0.05 MK) capturing the chromosphere and transition region, showing bright plasma prominences and filament eruptions.

terms.name: SDO AIA 131 Å
terms.desc: EUV channel (Fe VIII/Fe XXI, ~10 MK) optimized for tracking intense solar flares and active magnetic reconnection regions.

terms.name: SDO HMI Magnetogram
terms.desc: High-resolution full-disk map of the Sun's photospheric line-of-sight magnetic field polarity (positive/white = outward, negative/black = inward).

terms.name: SOHO LASCO C2 & C3
terms.desc: White-light coronagraphs that artificially occult the bright solar disk to track the outer solar corona and Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) out to 32 solar radii.

terms.name: Coronal Mass Ejection (CME)
terms.desc: A massive expulsion of billions of tons of magnetized solar plasma and magnetic field erupting from the Sun into interplanetary space.

terms.name: Solar Wind Speed & Proton Density
terms.desc: Key telemetry indicators of the supersonic stream of charged particles flowing outward from the Sun (typical speed: 300–800 km/s; density: 1–30 protons/cm³).

terms.name: GOES X-Ray Flux & Flare Classes (A, B, C, M, X)
terms.desc: Logarithmic classification of solar flares based on 0.1–0.8 nm peak X-ray emission: X-class denotes extreme flares capable of planet-wide radio blackouts.

terms.name: Sunspot & Solar Cycle 25
terms.desc: A cooler, dark photospheric magnetic patch with an ~11-year periodicity driven by the Sun's internal dynamo; Cycle 25 is the current solar cycle reaching maximum activity in 2024–2026.

terms.name: Coronal Heating Paradox
terms.desc: The long-standing astrophysical enigma of why the solar corona (>1,000,000 K) is hundreds of times hotter than the underlying visible photosphere (5,778 K).

terms.name: Constellation Lines & Art
terms.desc: Geometric lines connecting recognized asterism stars, paired with classical and mythological artistic figures overlaid on the sky.

terms.name: Azimuthal (Alt-Az) Coordinate Grid
terms.desc: Local observer-centric coordinate system: Altitude measures angular height above the horizon (0° to 90°), and Azimuth measures compass bearing (0° North to 360°).

terms.name: Equatorial Coordinate Grid
terms.desc: Earth-axis aligned celestial sphere grid tracking Right Ascension (0h to 24h) and Declination (-90° to +90°) independent of local observer location.

terms.name: Atmospheric Extinction & Refraction
terms.desc: Optical bending and dimming of light as starlight passes through Earth's atmospheric layers, most pronounced near the horizon.

terms.name: Deep-Sky Objects (DSOs)
terms.desc: Non-stellar objects beyond our solar system, including star clusters, nebulae, and external galaxies.

terms.name: Red Night Mode
terms.desc: Low-intensity red light display mode designed to protect rhodopsin photopigments in human eyes, preserving natural night-vision adaptation.

terms.name: Sidereal Time vs. Solar Time
terms.desc: Time measured relative to distant background stars (approx. 23h 56m 4s per Earth rotation) versus standard solar noon time.

terms.name: Parker Solar Probe
terms.desc: NASA spacecraft flying through the Sun's outer corona at record-breaking speeds (>600,000 km/h) to investigate coronal heating and solar wind acceleration.

terms.name: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)
terms.desc: Premier 6.5-meter infrared space observatory stationed at Sun-Earth L2 studying early cosmic galaxy formation, exoplanet atmospheres, and stellar birth.

terms.name: Hubble Space Telescope (HST)
terms.desc: Pioneering optical, ultraviolet, and near-infrared observatory in low Earth orbit since 1990.

terms.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)
terms.desc: NASA orbiter providing high-resolution 0.5-meter optical surface cartography, laser altimetry, and thermal mapping of the Moon.

terms.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO)
terms.desc: High-resolution imaging and atmospheric sounding satellite investigating Martian geology, surface ice, and landing sites via the HiRISE camera.

terms.name: Chandra X-Ray Observatory
terms.desc: NASA Great Observatory detecting X-ray emissions from black hole accretion disks, quasars, supernova remnants, and colliding galaxy clusters.

terms.name: TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite)
terms.desc: NASA space telescope executing an all-sky photometric survey to discover transiting exoplanets around bright nearby stars.

terms.name: Solar Orbiter
terms.desc: ESA/NASA spacecraft taking the first high-resolution images of the Sun's polar regions while tracking heliospheric magnetic flux.

terms.name: Ephemeris Telemetry (JPL Horizons)
terms.desc: Precision computational datasets computing position, velocity vectors, orbital state, and observational geometry for spacecraft and natural bodies.

terms.name: Astro-Copilot AI
terms.desc: Contextual astronomical assistant powered by LLM reasoning, trained to interpret observational telemetry, ephemeris data, and sky phenomena in real time.

terms.name: Virtual Observatory (VO)
terms.desc: An open, distributed international framework enabling researchers and the public to seamlessly query, visualize, and cross-match multi-agency astrophysical datasets.

terms.name: Bortle Scale
terms.desc: A standardized nine-level numerical scale (Class 1 = pristine dark sky, Class 9 = inner-city sky) quantifying light pollution and night-sky visibility.
